answer: Six scrolls. Six seals pressed in wax by hands that read every line before stamping. Proof of archivist seal via royal archive is a seal of that kind: a seal the royal archive stamps only after the archivist catalogues a scroll he actually read. The ember is the wax: melted, and the seal holds or the scroll is a forgery. 6 invented seals take 6 archivists and 6 winters the archivist never opened a scroll; the copper of each is the ribbon, tied round a scroll never read, the sable the vault where the unsealed scrolls rot.
